sources.title: Persepolis I: Structures, Reliefs, Inscriptions (Oriental Institute Publications 68)
sources.author: Erich F. Schmidt
sources.publisher: University of Chicago Press / Oriental Institute
sources.note: Full volume (OI Publications 68, 1953) opened as the ISAC open-access PDF 2026-10-31. Pages cited were checked against the printed page headers: p. 68 (Xerxes' gate: composite capitals topped by addorsed bulls; beams in the saddle), p. 80 (Apadana porticoes: north portico and hall bulls, west bulls, east addorsed horned leonine monsters), p. 81 (fragments of the eastern portico's leonine capitals), p. 137 (man-bull and bull capitals carry a rosette neckband). Cite for description only; the PDF is not for reuse beyond citation.

sources.title: Women with Mustaches and Men without Beards
sources.author: Afsaneh Najmabadi
sources.note: Read through the author's Introduction as posted on iranian.com (June 2005), which previews chapter 3 on the lion and sun; the full book/PDF could not be opened, so there are no print page numbers. Cited only for statements made in the Introduction: the emblem "first formally adopted in 1836", the changing sun face (Qajar face; most facial markings lost by the early twentieth century, erased by the mid-1930s; geometrised in the 1970s; discarded 1979). The earlier "unique success" quotation could NOT be found and was cut.

sources.title: Flags i. Of Persia
sources.author: Alireza Shapur Shahbazi
sources.note: Opened in full 2026-10-31 (last updated 2 June 2016). Basis for the history of the lion-and-sun emblem and flag. Note Iranica says the Qajar state had an official lion-and-sun flag from the time of Fath-Ali Shah; Najmabadi (najmabadi2005) dates the emblem's formal adoption to 1836. Sources differ; the pages say only "in official use in the Qajar period".

sources.title: The Supplementary Fundamental Laws of Persia, 7 October 1907, Article 5
sources.author: Persian Constitution (English translation as reproduced by the Abdorrahman Boroumand Center)
sources.note: Article 5: "The official colours of the Persian flag are green, white and red, with the emblem of the Lion and the sun." Translator not named on the page; quote is from that translation.

sources.title: Crown Jewels of Persia
sources.author: Patricia Jellicoe
sources.publisher: Encyclopaedia Iranica (online edition), vol. VI, fasc. 4, pp. 426-430
sources.note: Opened in full 2026-10-31 (updated 21 Aug 2013). Gives: transfer of the whole collection by law to Bank Melli on 25 Aban 1314 / 16 Nov 1935 (held as collateral for banknotes; now Central Bank of Iran); coronation of Mohammad-Reza Shah on 4 Aban 1346 / 26 Oct 1967 with the Pahlavi crown commissioned by Reza Shah for 1926. The earlier draft said 1937 (from Wikipedia); Iranica is preferred.

sources.title: Shiraz Arts Festival
sources.author: Hormoz Farhat
sources.note: Opened in full 2026-10-31. Eleven consecutive festivals from 1967 (final one 1977), at Shiraz and Persepolis; "owed its conception to the ideas put forth by the queen of Iran, Shahbanu Farah". Includes dated festival programmes.

sources.title: Education xvii. Higher Education
sources.author: David Menashri
sources.publisher: Encyclopaedia Iranica (online edition), vol. VIII, fasc. 2, pp. 216-219
sources.note: Opened 2026-10-31. A law establishing the university was introduced in the Majles on 13 March 1934; Tehran University was inaugurated on 4 February 1935. Resolves the 1934/1935 discrepancy (law vs opening).

sources.title: A Monument of Destiny: Envisioning a Nation's Past, Present, and Future Through Shahyad/Azadi
sources.author: Khashayar Hemmati
sources.note: Full text opened 2026-10-31 (PDF via summit.sfu.ca). Gives the inauguration as the evening of 16 October 1971 (citing Ettela'at, 16 Oct 1971); Amanat's entry chosen in a national competition announced 1 Sept 1966; the celebrations ran from Pasargadae and Persepolis to Tehran. A 2025 article in Iranian Studies (doi 10.1017/irn.2025.25) is reported in search results to give 17 October for the shah's arrival; NOT opened, so the day is qualified.

sources.title: Abbas, At the tomb of Cyrus the Great, celebrations of the 2500th anniversary of the monarchy (1971, printed 2016), curatorial notes
sources.author: Los Angeles County Museum of Art
sources.note: LACMA M.2016.199.4. Curatorial note: "The festivities opened on October 12th, when the Shah paid homage to Cyrus at his mausoleum at Pasargadae." Cites Komaroff 2018. Replaces Wikipedia for the opening day.

sources.title: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art (project page, 1967-1976)
sources.author: Kamran Diba (architect)
sources.note: Architect's own account (primary, but self-description). Says the project was initiated by him, dates it 1967-1976, and that he served as interim director for eighteen months once the building was finished. Does not name any co-architect; the earlier "with Nader Ardalan" claim could not be sourced and was removed.

sources.title: Tehran Museum of Contemporary Art (TMoCA)
sources.author: A. Cubbon
sources.publisher: The Routledge Encyclopedia of Modernism (Taylor & Francis)
sources.note: doi 10.4324/9781135000356-REM2095-1. Says Empress Farah Pahlavi inaugurated TMoCA in 1977 and that Kamran Diba designed it.
